title: The inverse image $p_X^*$ from the point
statement:
For a scheme $X$ with structure morphism $\pi_X\colon X\to\Spec\Z$, define
$$
p_X^*:=\pi_X^*\circ p^*\colon\Sh(*_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)\longrightarrow\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab),
$$
where $p^*$ is the inverse-image functor of [def-sfb-point-upper-star] and
$\pi_X^*$ is the pullback of [def-sfb-finite-upper-star] for $\mathcal A=\Ab$.
For the sheafified objectwise tensor products over $\mathbf Z$ of
[sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], $p_X^*$ is strong monoidal and braided.

proof.text:
Put $P=p^*$, $Q=\pi_X^*$ and $R=Q\circ P$. By [lem-sfb-point-upper-star-braided], $P$ is strong monoidal and braided. By [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-braided], $Q$ is strong symmetric monoidal, hence strong monoidal and braided. These statements apply with the coefficient category $\Ab$ and the arbitrary scheme morphism $\pi_X$; no finiteness assumption on $X$ or $\pi_X$ is required.
Write $\epsilon^P,\mu^P$ and $\epsilon^Q,\mu^Q$ for their unit and tensor comparison isomorphisms in the direction $\mathbf 1\to P\mathbf 1$ and $PA\otimes PB\to P(A\otimes B)$. Give $R$ the comparisons
$$
\epsilon^R=Q(\epsilon^P)\circ\epsilon^Q,\qquad
\mu^R_{A,B}=Q(\mu^P_{A,B})\circ\mu^Q_{PA,PB}.
$$
They are invertible, since functors preserve inverses and composites of invertible maps are invertible. Expanding either side of each associativity or unit coherence identity for these maps, naturality of $\mu^Q$ moves the maps $Q(\mu^P)$ or $Q(\epsilon^P)$ together; the remaining equalities are $Q$ applied to the corresponding identity for $P$, followed by the corresponding identity for $Q$. Thus these maps give the composite strong monoidal structure. For the braiding $\beta$, its compatibility is explicitly
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mu^R_{B,A}\circ\beta_{RA,RB}
&=Q(\mu^P_{B,A})\circ\mu^Q_{PB,PA}\circ\beta_{QPA,QPB}\\
&=Q(\mu^P_{B,A}\circ\beta_{PA,PB})\circ\mu^Q_{PA,PB}\\
&=Q(P(\beta_{A,B})\circ\mu^P_{A,B})\circ\mu^Q_{PA,PB}\\
&=R(\beta_{A,B})\circ\mu^R_{A,B}.
\end{aligned}
$$
The second equality is the braided identity for $Q$, the third is that for $P$, and the last is functoriality. Hence the defined $p_X^*=R$ is strong monoidal and braided.
